title: Children's combined dress (part 2 out of 2)
description: In this final part, we sew the fifth -youth skirt and sew the border.   The first part of the lesson: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wcz5wilt9rs&feature=youtu.be  Playlist with border options: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=plwm_gxwybe64ip_voyyyy-pd6kbk4tgj   Table with standard children's sizes: http://veryhappysocks.blogspot.com.au/2015/06/0-3.html  Look for me on Instagram: https://instagram.com/nina.spica_handmade/  My group VKontakte: http://vk.com/public96260867  I'm on Blogger: http://veryhappysocks.blogspot.com.au/

asr.full_text: And in this video we're going to continue to work on this kind of kids' combination. the dress in the first part we tied up in this same part we're going to do the bottom before. buy the fabric you have to do all the calculations to avoid the unpleasant surprises so that you know exactly how much fabric you have going on the skirt itself the skirt is very simple you can do it right away. So you have to have the same number or you have to have more than your hip size. So that the skirt goes well because it's only on the rubber without the strap. So you have to take this into account. Let's say I have a waistline of 50 centimeters. I'm adding 20 centimeters. I get 70 this number you have to divide by 3.14 in the end I get somewhere about 22 centimeters. Now what we need to do is determine the length of the skirt. You add a few centimeters to the skirt. You add a few centimeters to the skirt. I add five centimeters to your skirt. The fabric will bend down here. twice. So you can measure how much you're going to use on it. And then you pinch the fabric so that it's straight. So you're going to put it down. Then you're going to make a mark and cut it. When you cut your piece out of the fabric, you're going to cut the yarn right away. And then you're going to cut the yarn, so it's going to be much more convenient to work with it later on and after the yarn is cut, it's going to be very convenient to do the measurements on the yarn. So how exactly do I do this. So that the calculations are as accurate as possible? I take the usual and apply it. I want to show you the best way to sew the seams and sew the skirt itself. First you sew the seams down the bottom, which is if you do everything by hand, then you use the seams. Then the top part where you have the rubber, then you sew the seams up the top carefully so that there's room for the rubber here. And then you can sew the back seams. First you sew the back seams, and I'll show you all this a little later, then you sew the back seams and you eat the seams together and then you just sew the seams so that the seams are a little bit of a piece of a piece of rubber back and then you look back at the seams and then you see the seams and then you see the seams back and then you see the seams back and then you see the seams back and then you see the seams back and then you see the seams back and then you see the seams back and then you see the seams back and then you see the seams back and then you see the seams back and then you see the seams back seams. So you're sewing the top, then you're sewing the back. I do it with these little vertical seams. And then I'm going to go back to the seam with a needle. And then I'm going back to the seam. And then I'm going back to the seam. You connect both parts with a pin and you sew the outer side with a secret seam. You do the same thing with the fabric. You sew the first part with a pin and then you sew it completely. And the last step in my work is to swallow. I'll work in two temperature modes. I swallow the skirt at the maximum temperature with a good dressing. That is, the maximum temperature possible, because I have cotton here. I put the maximum and maximum evaporation. You can also sew the fabric in advance. I'll use the average temperature to swallow the fabric and the top of the product. And usually, I'll use the ordinary fabric to help with the marble. I'll use marble instead of the ordinary fabric. And then you're going to have to do some kind of stuff like that, and you're not going to touch it, and you're going to have to invite the motivators.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because its observable purpose is an instructional sewing and crochet project for assembling a child's dress, including measuring fabric, cutting, sewing seams, and finishing. The sampled frame of hands sewing patterned fabric and the completed garment is consistent with that tutorial context. Although the description includes links to related lessons and social-media pages, the available video evidence does not establish payment, data submission, or participation in a harmful scheme.
